memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean till evening. Anyone who sleeps or eats in the house must wash their clothes." - Lev 14:46-47 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The house is shut up under examination, and God warns His people plainly: do not casually walk in. Sleep there, eat there, and you carry something out with you.

There is ordinary wisdom in this that we can miss. What we live inside affects us. Not dramatically, not immediately, but steadily — through sleeping and eating, through the daily unremarkable hours.

Think of the environments you spend time in. The group chat that runs on gossip. The workplace culture where dishonesty is normal and everyone shrugs. The friendship that has become a place where you always end up complaining. You may not agree with any of it. But you are sleeping and eating there.

Paul quotes a proverb the Corinthians would have known: bad company corrupts good character (1 Cor 15:33). And the very first psalm draws the picture — blessed is the one who does not walk in step with the wicked or stand in the way that sinners take or sit in the company of mockers (Ps 1:1). Walk, stand, sit. It gets more settled each time.

This is not a call to fear people or withdraw from the world. Jesus ate with sinners. It is a call to be awake about what we are marinating in.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What environment are you regularly "sleeping and eating" in?
2. Has it shaped you in ways you did not choose?
3. What is one atmosphere you should step out of this month?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, make me alert to the atmospheres I live in. Give me wisdom to remain among people who need You without absorbing what dishonours You. Amen.
